findings.title: Integer overflow in Wagner-Fischer matrix size computation in editDist3Core()
findings.message: In editDist3Core(), the Wagner-Fischer edit-distance matrix dimensions are computed as 'n = (f.n+1)*(n2+1)' where both f.n (FROM string length) and n2 (TO string length) are plain 'int' values with no upper-bound guard. When an attacker supplies two sufficiently long strings to the editdist3() SQL function, the multiplication overflows a 32-bit signed integer, yielding a small or negative value for n. The subsequent heap allocation 'nByte = n*sizeof(m[0]) + sizeof(a2[0])*n2' is then based on the corrupted n, so sqlite3_malloc64() allocates a far-too-small buffer; all subsequent matrix writes overflow that buffer, corrupting the heap. Even without a full overflow, the O(m×n) algorithm imposes unbounded CPU time for arbitrarily large inputs. The fix adds explicit guards 'if( n2>10000 ) return -2; if( f.n>10000 ) return -2;' before the matrix size computation.

related_locations.description: User-controlled SQL arguments zA/zB with lengths nA/nB are passed without size validation into editDist3FromStringNew() and editDist3Core(), allowing unbounded-length inputs to reach the vulnerable computation.

findings.suggestion: Add input size guards before the matrix size computation in editDist3Core(). The fix adds: 'if( n2>10000 ) return -2;' and 'if( f.n>10000 ) return -2;' immediately before 'n = (f.n+1)*(n2+1);', and handles the new return code -2 in the caller (editDist3SqlFunc) as sqlite3_result_error_toobig().

ground_truth.root_cause: No upper-bound validation is applied to the FROM or TO string lengths before performing the integer multiplication used to size the edit-distance matrix. Both f.n and n2 are 32-bit signed integers, so their product can overflow when each exceeds roughly 46,000 characters, yielding a corrupted allocation size.
